meta.structure_note: All color custom properties in this codebase live in exactly one file (frontend/app/globals.css), declared twice each: once in :root (light theme) and once in [data-theme="dark"] (dark theme overrides). There are two parallel, coexisting palettes rather than one: a 'core' set (--color-*, the original app-wide primitives used in chat/login/pricing/shared badges) and an 'admin' set (--admin-*, a second palette ported from a separate 'Theke Admin design' prototype and layered on top of the core set for the sidebar, top bar, and every admin-facing panel/dashboard). This file preserves that real split (tokens.core / tokens.admin / tokens.chat) instead of forcing everything into a single flat list.
changelog_since_last_export: Removed 3 dead tokens that were declared but never referenced: --color-text-on-accent, --admin-construction-on-dark, --admin-tax-on-dark. (A 4th dead token, --gradient-sidebar, was also removed from the CSS but was never part of this JSON export - it's a gradient, not a flat color.)

Unified --admin-danger and --error-red (both were #c62828 in light mode, and both fell back to the same value in dark mode) into a single --admin-danger token. Survivor chosen for broader existing usage (admin badges, delete/suspend confirmations, failed-sync status - 13 call sites vs. --error-red's 6 form-validation-only call sites) and because it doesn't bake a hue into the token's own name.

Unified --admin-info and --color-primary-hover (both were #2a6fdb in light mode, and this pairing was actually already an intentional documented choice, not an accidental duplicate) into a single --color-primary-hover token. Survivor chosen because it's the foundational core primitive powering the universal .btn-primary:hover rule and already had a proper, tested dark-mode value (#5c7dc4) - renaming that foundational rule to an --admin-* token would have been an architectural regression even though --admin-info had more raw call sites.

Added genuine dark-mode values for admin.status.success (#2e7d32 -> #4ade80) and admin.status.warning (#f57f17 -> #fb923c), matching the brightening pattern their core.status siblings already use. admin.status.danger is explicitly restated with the SAME value in both themes (deliberate - matches core.status.danger's own established 'constant across themes' pattern, not an oversight).

Declared --color-surface-hover properly (was previously referenced with an undeclared fallback, rgba(0,0,0,0.04), invisible in dark mode). New value: rgba(21,29,72,0.05) light / rgba(255,255,255,0.07) dark.

Added a new token, admin.text.text_on_dark (--admin-text-on-dark), consolidating three previously ad hoc hardcoded values (#fff, #b7c2dc, #d8e0f0) used for secondary/body text on permanently-dark navy surfaces (sidebar footer role label + sign-out icon, DataSourcesPanel's active frequency-pill label, VerticalEditorPanel's system-prompt textarea text). Genuinely maximal-contrast name/heading text on the same surfaces (the user's own name in the sidebar footer, the avatar initial) was left pointed at the existing core.text.on_primary token instead, preserving the footer's existing two-tier visual hierarchy rather than flattening it.

Fixed a hardcoded #d8d0c2 (a leftover from the old warm-beige palette) on the collapsed sidebar's inactive vertical-switcher dot - now uses admin.surface.card_border, the sidebar's own established border token.
Net token count: 59 -> 56 (-3 dead, -1 danger merge, -1 info merge, +1 surface_hover, +1 text_on_dark).

Follow-up pass: swept the whole frontend for remaining raw hex in CSS/inline-style contexts (every one was a 'text/icon sitting on a colored fill' case, same role as core.text.on_primary) and repointed them at that existing token instead of adding anything new: Sidebar.tsx's vertical-switcher active-segment text+dot, Sidebar.module.css's .navChildItemActive text and .avatar border, TopHeader.module.css/StatCard.module.css/AttentionCard.module.css's avatar/icon-badge text, SessionExpiryToast.module.css and SubscriptionsPanel.module.css's status-pill text, and two inline danger-button labels in CompaniesPanel.tsx/DocumentsPanel.tsx. Also replaced a hand-picked dark-theme background (Sidebar.module.css's .navItemActive, was a hardcoded #25344f) with the same color-mix(...) pattern the light-theme rule right above it already uses, just mixed against the dark surface instead of white - ties it back to --admin-accent-navy instead of an unrelated hex. Removed two now-redundant var(..., #fallback) hex fallbacks in pricing.module.css (the token they fell back from is always declared).

Correction to the follow-up pass above: 2 of the call sites it repointed at core.text.on_primary were actually background/border properties, not text - Sidebar.tsx's .switcherDotInline active fill and Sidebar.module.css's .avatar ring border. A background/border color and a text color are different design-system concerns even when the current hex happens to match (#ffffff in both cases here), so a rebrand could need to change one without the other. Split those 2 call sites out into a new token, core.background.on_primary, rather than continuing to borrow the text token. Grouped both into ONE new token (not two) since they share identical value and semantic role; core.text.on_primary's remaining ~11 call sites were re-verified as genuine `color:`/icon-foreground usages and were left as-is.
Net token count: 56 -> 57 (+1 core.background.on_primary; no removals).

Chat v2 redesign follow-up pass: added chat.citation_tag_bg/citation_tag_bg_hover as two genuinely new tokens (#eef0f3/#f3f5f9 light) - the source-tag pill bg and source-row hover bg were both previously aliasing core.background.surface_alt, which read close to but not exactly the design spec's two distinct values. Also converted chat.disclaimer_bg/disclaimer_border/disclaimer_text from aliases of the shared core.status.warning_bg/admin.status.warning_border/core.text.muted into dedicated chat-only tokens matching the v2 design's exact values (#fbf6e9/#efe4c4/#7a6425) - repointing the shared warning tokens themselves would have repainted every other warning banner/badge app-wide as an unintended side effect of a chat-only visual pass. The separate chat.disclaimer_icon token was folded into chat.disclaimer_text (one warm-brown tone now covers both, per the v2 spec, replacing the previous amber icon/muted-text split). Scoped to the desktop .disclaimerBar only - the mobile .disclaimerMobile variant is out of scope for this pass and still uses the shared warning tokens.

That same pass also silently dropped chat.citation_chip_bg/citation_chip_text with no changelog entry - a real bug, not a rename. Those two entries documented the pre-v2 numbered citation badge (markup was `.citations li`/`.citationLink`), itself an alias of core.background.surface_alt/core.text.muted. The v2 redesign replaced that markup with `.sourceRow`/`.sourceBadge`/`.sourceTag` - two DIFFERENT elements, per the v2 design: `.sourceBadge` (the numbered badge, e.g. "1") and `.sourceTag` (the source-type pill, e.g. "ΤΕΕ", a sibling element). chat.citation_tag_bg/citation_tag_bg_hover (added in the same pass, see entry above) correctly document `.sourceTag` and `.sourceRow:hover` - they are NOT a replacement for citation_chip_bg/text, despite landing in the same spot in this file's structure. `.sourceBadge` itself moved to a *different* existing pair, --color-accent-soft-bg/--color-accent-soft-text (#eaf0fb/#2f4b86 light, #22304c/#9db4e8 dark) - declared in globals.css since the original v2 redesign commit (a66793f) but never itself added to this export, on any pass, until now. That's the actual root cause: when `.sourceBadge` absorbed this already-undocumented pair's styling, there was no existing entry to redirect, so the numbered badge's color silently fell out of the export instead of being reassigned.

Fix: added core.brand.accent_soft_bg/accent_soft_text as new primitive entries for --color-accent-soft-bg/--color-accent-soft-text, used at 3 call sites in chat/chat.module.css: .assistantAvatar (the assistant-identity sparkle avatar), .sourceBadge (the numbered source-citation badge - the one formerly documented as chat.citation_chip_bg/text), and .activeProjectChip/.activeProjectChipLabel/.activeProjectChipValue/.activeProjectChipClear (the context-panel's active-project chip).

Also fixed: the previous entry's own net-count arithmetic was wrong (claimed '57 -> 61', actual result was 56) and design/color-tokens.md's header still said '61 tokens total' while separately still listing citation_chip_bg/text in its token table as if all four (chip + tag) coexisted - both files are regenerated together from this same pass so they can't drift apart like that again. Corrected net count: 56 -> 58 (+2 core.brand.accent_soft_bg/accent_soft_text; no other additions or removals in this pass - citation_chip_bg/text were already gone from the prior export, this pass only documents where that color role actually went).

Found while reviewing for this fix, NOT merged (flagging only, per explicit instruction to leave duplicate-hex merge decisions to design review, same as any other candidate in this file): core.brand.accent and core.status.warning hold the identical hex in BOTH themes (#ffa800/#ffcf00 light/dark). Unlike the --admin-danger/--error-red and --admin-info/--color-primary-hover merges earlier in this file's history, these are NOT being unified here - a rebrand could reasonably want the brand accent and a semantic warning color to diverge even though they happen to coincide today. Revisit only if a designer confirms these are meant to be the same token long-term.

Descriptiveness pass, wording-only (no tokens added or removed, still 58): audited every entry for whether `usage` states the actual CSS property (background / color / border / outline / stroke) at each of its call sites, not just a vague role name. Verified against the real CSS/TSX at every call site rather than assumed. 17 entries needed a fix, in two groups. Group A (12 tokens) are genuinely reused across MULTIPLE different CSS properties at different call sites on the SAME single custom property - not something to split into separate tokens (that would misrepresent one shared variable as independently adjustable per property/call-site, which is a real CSS change, out of scope here) - so each now states which property applies at which call site: admin.status.danger, admin.vertical.construction, admin.vertical.tax, core.status.info, admin.status.neutral, admin.status.success, admin.status.warning, core.brand.primary, core.brand.primary_hover, core.brand.link, core.status.purple, core.background.on_primary. Group B (5 tokens) were already single-property but the `usage` text named a role ('fill', 'accent', 'surface') without ever naming the CSS property itself - tightened to say `background`/`border` explicitly: core.brand.accent, core.brand.accent_hover, core.brand.accent_soft_bg, admin.brand.accent_navy, core.background.surface_alt, admin.surface.row_border. Also corrected several `used_in` lists that were missing real call sites found during this audit (components/LandingPage.module.css was undocumented for admin.vertical.construction/construction_bg/tax/tax_bg and core.brand.primary; components/SpendAlertsPanel.tsx and dashboard/CompanyActivityChart.tsx were undocumented for core.brand.primary and core.status.info respectively).
